name: black_hole_field
character: A field far larger than any room: 60 m across, a 30 m ceiling, and a tail long enough that a single struck note outlives the phrase it belongs to.
sources: Sabine's reverberation equation, RT60 = 0.161 V / A (knowledgebase/sound-design/acoustics-room.md): a 60 x 60 x 30 m plaster box has V = 108000 m3, so the 6.5 s tail here is the order of magnitude the geometry would give, not a measured room
ITU-R BS.775 / BS.2051 front-azimuth convention (-30, 0, +30 deg) supplies the speaker angles; the field's own box is project geometry, since no real hall of this size was measured
Air absorption from ISO 9613-1 at 18 C and 40 percent relative humidity: the 2.6 kHz minimum cutoff at far distance is the air-absorption shelf, not a mix decision

knowledgebase/sound-design/immersive-spatial.md section 2c: a room whose tail must change uses scene transitions on the space preset, so the crush and last-light transitions are written in the direction sheet and executed here
ESTIMATE: early tap gains, pre-delay law, late level -13 dB and the 10-tap order are starting values for a field this size; none has been measured
